name: Rashid Sunyaev
milestone_by_age_26: Completed Candidate of Sciences (PhD equivalent) in astrophysics from Moscow State University at age 25 in 1968, working under Yakov Zel'dovich at the Institute of Applied Mathematics of the USSR Academy of Sciences.
early_history_summary: Sunyaev studied physics at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology (MIPT) from 1960 to 1966, then completed his PhD in astrophysics at Moscow State University by 1968. He became a Junior Scientific Researcher at the Institute of Applied Mathematics under Zel'dovich, one of the Soviet Union's most prominent physicists.
family_context_summary: Born in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, USSR to a family of Tatar descent; specific family financial and occupational background not documented in reviewed sources.
primary_early_advantage_tags: MIPT, Zel'dovich mentorship, Soviet Academy of Sciences, astrophysics
evidence_summary: Sunyaev entered MIPT at 17 and completed his PhD in astrophysics by 25 under Yakov Zel'dovich at the Institute of Applied Mathematics. His access to MIPT and then to Zel'dovich's group at the USSR Academy of Sciences provided elite institutional and mentorship advantages. His landmark papers (SZ effect, Shakura-Sunyaev disk) came just after age 26, but his PhD and research position constituted a material milestone by 26. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born in Tashkent, Uzbekistan, USSR to a family of Tatar descent; family financial and occupational background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Emeritus Director and Scientific Member at the Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics in Garching, Germany; Chief Scientist at the Space Research Institute, Russian Academy of Sciences.

trajectory.event: Completed MS degree at the Moscow Institute of Physics and Technology.
Completed Candidate of Sciences (PhD) in astrophysics from Moscow State University and became Junior Scientific Researcher at the Institute of Applied Mathematics under Zel'dovich.
Co-authored the Sunyaev-Zel'dovich effect paper predicting baryon acoustic oscillations and acoustic peaks in the CMB.
Co-authored the seminal Shakura-Sunyaev accretion disk model with Nikolai Shakura.
Became Director of the Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics in Garching, Germany.
Awarded the Gruber Cosmology Prize.
Appointed Maureen and John Hendricks Visiting Professor at the Institute for Advanced Study, Princeton.

name: Valeri Kharlamov
milestone_by_age_26: Debuted for CSKA Moscow in the Soviet League at age 19 in 1967, and by age 26 had won multiple World Championship gold medals (1969-1973), been named Soviet League MVP (1972, 1973), and received the Merited Master of Sport title (1969).
early_history_summary: Kharlamov started skating at age 5, trained by his father Boris who played hockey himself. He joined CSKA Moscow's sports school at age 12 and made his senior team debut on October 22, 1967. After a brief demotion to Zvezda Chebarkul where he led the team in scoring with 34 goals in 32 games, he returned to CSKA and became a dominant player, scoring 37 goals in 42 games in his first full season.
family_context_summary: Born in Moscow to Boris Kharlamov, a factory mechanic at the Kommunar plant, and Begoñita (Carmen Orive Abad), a Basque refugee from the Spanish Civil War who worked at Aeroflot. Father Boris played hockey himself and trained Valeri from a young age.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father Boris Kharlamov played hockey and personally trained Valeri from age 5, providing direct domain coaching and early skill development.
primary_early_advantage_tags: CSKA Moscow, father-coach, Soviet hockey system, early skating, Kharlamov-Petrov-Mikhailov line
evidence_summary: Kharlamov was immersed in hockey from age 5, trained by his father who played the sport. He joined CSKA Moscow's sports school at 12 and made the senior team at 19. Despite a childhood rheumatic fever diagnosis, he became one of the Soviet League's dominant players by his early 20s, winning World Championships and being named MVP. The CSKA Moscow pipeline and the legendary Kharlamov-Petrov-Mikhailov line were key structural advantages.
starting_point: Born in Moscow to a factory mechanic father who played hockey and a Basque refugee mother who worked at Aeroflot; working-class family in the Soviet system.
current_position: Died on August 27, 1981 at age 33 in a car crash near Moscow; final role: star forward for CSKA Moscow and the Soviet national team.

trajectory.event: Debuted for CSKA Moscow in the Soviet League on October 22, 1967.
Named Merited Master of Sport and won first World Championship gold medal.
Named Soviet Championship League MVP and led the league in scoring; won Olympic gold at Sapporo and starred in the Summit Series against Canada.
Named Soviet League MVP for the second consecutive year.
Won Olympic gold at Innsbruck despite injuries from a car accident earlier that year.
Died in a car crash on August 27, 1981, along with his wife, while returning from their summer cottage.

name: Michel Pollentier
milestone_by_age_26: Turned professional in 1973 at age 22 and by age 26 won the 1977 Giro d'Italia, the Tour of Switzerland, and the Belgian Road Race Championship, having already finished 7th overall in the Tour de France in 1974 and 1976.
early_history_summary: Pollentier was a Belgian cyclist who knew his friend and fellow cyclist Freddy Maertens since their junior years. He turned professional in 1973 with the Flandria team and served as a domestique for Maertens before emerging as a top rider in his own right, notably beating Eddy Merckx in a Tour de France time trial in 1974.

primary_early_advantage_tags: Belgian cycling culture, Flandria team, Maertens partnership
evidence_summary: Pollentier grew up in Belgium, the heartland of professional cycling, and trained with Freddy Maertens from their junior years. He turned professional in 1973 with Flandria and quickly proved himself by beating Eddy Merckx in a Tour de France time trial at age 23. By 26 he won the Giro d'Italia. Family background is not documented in reviewed sources.

name: Jamie Foxx
milestone_by_age_26: Cast as a featured player on the nationally broadcast Fox sketch comedy show In Living Color in 1991 at age 23, providing a material breakthrough in entertainment by age 26.
early_history_summary: Foxx was raised by his adoptive grandparents in Terrell, Texas, where he began playing piano at age 5 and was a part-time pianist and choir leader at his church. He played football and basketball in high school and received a classical piano scholarship to United States International University. During college, he began performing standup comedy at open mic nights, taking the name Jamie Foxx to get stage time.
family_context_summary: Born Eric Marlon Bishop in Terrell, Texas, and adopted as an infant by his maternal grandparents Esther Marie (a domestic worker and nursery operator) and Mark Talley (a yard worker). His birth father worked as a stockbroker. He was raised in a racially segregated black community with a strict Baptist upbringing.
parent_family_domain_summary: Adoptive grandmother was a domestic worker and nursery operator; adoptive grandfather was a yard worker. No documented family domain expertise in entertainment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: piano from age 5, church performance, comedy open mics, In Living Color
evidence_summary: Foxx was raised by his adoptive grandparents in a segregated community in Terrell, Texas, with no family connections in entertainment. He developed piano skills from age 5 and comedic talent from childhood, performing at church and school. After winning a piano scholarship to USIU, he began doing standup comedy, which led to his casting on In Living Color at age 23. His early advantage was self-created through persistent practice in music and comedy.
starting_point: Born in Terrell, Texas and adopted by his maternal grandparents — a domestic worker/nursery operator and a yard worker — in a racially segregated black community.
current_position: Award-winning actor, comedian, and musician; recovered from a serious medical emergency in 2023 and returned to acting; estimated net worth approximately $170 million.

name: Christopher Nolan

name: Tom Okker
milestone_by_age_26: Became Dutch national tennis champion from 1964 through 1968 starting at age 20, won two gold medals at the 1965 Maccabiah Games, and reached the final of the 1968 US Open at age 24.
early_history_summary: Okker was born in Amsterdam to a Jewish father who survived the Nazi occupation by going into hiding. He began considering tennis as a career after winning junior championships, became Dutch champion from 1964, and trained in Australia with other young tennis players. In 1968, his first year as a registered professional, he won the Italian Open and reached the US Open final.
family_context_summary: Born in Amsterdam; Jewish on his father's side. His father was imprisoned by the Nazis during World War II but survived by assuming another man's identity and going into hiding.

name: Víctor Jara
milestone_by_age_26: No material milestone by age 26 found; Jara was a member of the University of Chile choir and the folk group Cuncumén by his mid-20s, but his notable career as a theater director and solo recording artist began in the 1960s, with his first album in 1966 at age 34.

family_context_summary: Born to Manuel Jara, an illiterate tenant farmer, and Amanda Martínez, a folk singer and herbal remedy seller of Mapuche ancestry. His father was prone to violence and drinking. Mother died when Víctor was 15, leaving him adrift.
parent_family_domain_summary: Mother Amanda Martínez was a folk singer and guitar player who inspired Víctor's musical interest and provided early exposure to Chilean folk traditions.

name: Bong Joon-ho
milestone_by_age_26: Made short films that were invited to screen at international film festivals (Vancouver, Hong Kong) while at the Korean Academy of Film Arts, with his thesis film Incoherence (1994) attracting significant attention from the Korean film community by age 25.
early_history_summary: Bong grew up in an artistic family in Daegu and Seoul, South Korea. His father was a graphic design professor and his maternal grandfather was the celebrated novelist Park Tae-won. He majored in sociology at Yonsei University, co-founded the filmmaking club Yellow Door, and was accepted to the Korean Academy of Film Arts (KAFA), where he made several acclaimed short films.
family_context_summary: Born in Daegu, South Korea to Bong Sang-gyun, a graphic design professor and first-generation Korean graphic designer, and Park So-young, a housewife. His maternal grandfather was Park Tae-won, a celebrated Korean modernist novelist. He has three older siblings, including a brother who is an English professor and a sister who teaches fashion styling.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a graphic design professor and industrial designer; maternal grandfather was one of Korea's most important modernist novelists. Strong artistic and intellectual family environment.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father design professor, grandfather novelist, KAFA, Yellow Door, artistic family
evidence_summary: Bong grew up in an exceptionally artistic family: his father was a pioneering graphic design professor and his maternal grandfather was Park Tae-won, one of Korea's most celebrated modernist novelists. He co-founded the Yellow Door filmmaking club at Yonsei University and was accepted to KAFA, Korea's top film school, where his thesis film Incoherence attracted significant attention. His short films screened at international festivals by age 25-26. The combination of artistic family heritage and elite film education provided strong early advantages.
starting_point: Born in Daegu, South Korea to a graphic design professor father and a housewife mother; maternal grandfather was the celebrated novelist Park Tae-won; artistic and intellectual middle-class family.
current_position: South Korean filmmaker and Academy Award-winning director; last film Mickey 17 released in 2025; widely regarded as one of the world's leading directors.

Parasite won the Palme d'Or at Cannes and became the first non-English-language film to win the Academy Award for Best Picture.
Released Mickey 17, his third English-language feature.

name: Steven Seagal
milestone_by_age_26: Moved to Japan at age 17 in 1969 to study martial arts, received his 1st dan in aikido in 1974 at age 22, and by age 26 was running the Tenshin Aikido Dojo in Osaka as the first westerner to operate an aikido dojo in Japan.
early_history_summary: Seagal was born in Lansing, Michigan and moved to Fullerton, California at age 5. He began studying martial arts at age 7 under Fumio Demura and later aikido under Harry Ishisaka. At 17, he traveled to Japan to further his martial arts training, received his 1st dan from Koichi Tohei in 1974, married Miyako Fujitani, and assumed direction of his wife's family's aikido dojo in Osaka.
family_context_summary: Born in Lansing, Michigan to Samuel Seagal, a mathematics teacher, and Patricia Anne Fisher, a medical technician. Family moved to Fullerton, California when he was 5. No documented family martial arts background.

primary_early_advantage_tags: early martial arts training, Japan immersion, dojo operation, Demura and Ishisaka mentors
evidence_summary: Seagal began martial arts at age 7 in California under notable instructors Fumio Demura and Harry Ishisaka. At 17, he moved to Japan to pursue aikido full-time, receiving his 1st dan in 1974 and eventually running his wife's family dojo in Osaka as the first westerner to operate an aikido dojo in Japan. His acting career came much later (1988 at age 36). The key early advantage was sustained mentorship and immersion in Japanese martial arts culture.
starting_point: Born in Lansing, Michigan to a mathematics teacher father and a medical technician mother; family moved to Fullerton, California when he was 5; working-class to middle-class background.
current_position: American actor and martial artist; career has shifted largely to direct-to-video productions; holds Russian and Serbian citizenship; estimated net worth approximately $16 million.
